h1: Retaining Wall Contractor in Aylmer, Ontario
intro: Aylmer's flat farmland and agricultural roots mean most retaining walls here manage water and drainage grade rather than a steep slope. We build accordingly, with drainage as the priority on every job.
terrainNote: Aylmer is mostly flat, drained farmland, so retaining wall problems here are more often about controlling a drainage ditch grade change or a rural laneway than a hillside.
driveNote: Aylmer is about 40 minutes southeast of London, usually via Highway 4 and Highway 3.

blocks.text: Aylmer does not have the ravines or river valleys we see in London or St. Thomas, but flat, tile-drained farmland brings its own grading challenges. Rural properties around the Talbot Line often need a retaining wall to manage a drainage ditch, a raised driveway approach, or the grade change between a field and a homestead.

In town, residential lots near John Street and the older Aylmer core are generally modest in size, so retaining walls here tend to be smaller, focused on garden beds, short driveway sections, or leveling a small backyard rather than managing a major slope.

We regularly build retaining walls on Elgin County farm properties around Aylmer to hold back a laneway grade, protect a barn foundation from runoff, or create a level equipment pad. These jobs often use larger armour stone or heavy timber because the priority is durability under vehicle and equipment loads, not appearance.

items: Armour stone for farm laneways and equipment pad edges
Timber for lower-cost rural grade changes
Segmental block for in-town residential gardens and driveways
Poured concrete where a wall needs to support a structure or hold a specific engineered load

items.title: Assess the water
items.text: We look at where surface water and any drainage tile currently run before deciding on wall placement.

items.title: Base below frost depth
items.text: A compacted granular base is set below frost depth regardless of whether the site is rural or in town.

items.title: Weeping tile and stone
items.text: Perforated weeping tile ties into drainage stone behind the wall to move water away, not trap it.

items.title: Build to the load
items.text: Farm walls near equipment traffic get heavier material and a wider base than a garden wall.

items.title: Grade to existing drainage
items.text: We finish the grade so it works with, not against, the property's existing drainage pattern.

sections.heading: Permits in the Town of Aylmer

blocks.text: The Town of Aylmer requires a building permit for retaining walls over about 1 metre, consistent with the Ontario Building Code. Agricultural properties can have additional considerations depending on whether the wall is near a drainage tile system or a municipal drain, and we check this before quoting rural work.
Municipal drains are common around Aylmer farmland; a wall built too close to one without checking first can create a bigger problem than it solves.

sections.heading: What a Wall Costs in Aylmer

blocks.text: In-town block walls in Aylmer run about $200 to $350 per linear foot installed, the same range as the rest of our service area. Rural and farm-related walls are priced based on material and load requirements rather than a simple per-foot rate, since armour stone and heavy-duty bases cost more than a residential garden wall. As always, assessments are free.

Aylmer's agricultural economy means access to some rural sites is easiest outside the peak growing season, and we plan around planting and harvest timing when a wall project sits near active cropland. This is rarely an issue for in-town residential jobs near John Street, but it matters on working farm properties along the Talbot Line.

We also see a fair number of Aylmer projects tied to drainage improvements more broadly, where a retaining wall is one part of a larger plan to move water off a property correctly. Where that is the case, we coordinate wall placement with whatever tile or ditch work is already planned rather than treating the wall as a separate project.

sections.heading: Why Aylmer Property Owners Call Us

blocks.text: Word about a reliable contractor travels between neighbouring farm properties, and much of our Aylmer-area work comes from referrals along the Talbot Line and the concession roads around town. Farm owners tend to want a straightforward answer about durability and cost per job, not a sales pitch, and that is how we approach every rural quote.

We also keep spare capacity for smaller, urgent rural repairs, like a laneway edge that has washed out after a heavy rain, since agricultural operations often cannot wait weeks for a fix that affects daily equipment movement.

We understand that a retaining wall on an Elgin County farm property is a working structure first, and we build to that standard rather than treating every job like a suburban landscape wall. In town, we bring the same drainage-first approach to smaller residential projects, and either way you get a clear written quote with no pressure to book on the spot.
If you are weighing armour stone against timber for a rural Aylmer property, our /natural-stone-retaining-walls page covers where heavier stone earns its cost.

faqs.q: Do you build retaining walls on farm properties near Aylmer?
faqs.a: Yes, this is regular work for us in Elgin County. We build laneway, equipment pad and drainage-related walls using armour stone or heavy timber suited to agricultural loads.

faqs.q: Does my Aylmer property have a municipal drain nearby?
faqs.a: It is worth checking before any wall work, since a wall built too close to a municipal drain can affect its function. We confirm this during the site visit for rural projects.

faqs.q: What kind of retaining walls do in-town Aylmer properties need?
faqs.a: Usually smaller garden, driveway or backyard leveling walls, since most residential lots in Aylmer are modest in size and relatively flat compared to river valley towns nearby.

faqs.q: How much does a retaining wall cost in Aylmer?
faqs.a: In-town block walls run about $200 to $350 per linear foot, matching our other service areas. Rural and farm walls are priced by material and load rather than a flat per-foot rate.

faqs.q: How far is Aylmer from your shop?
faqs.a: About 40 minutes from London via Highway 4 and Highway 3, and we schedule Aylmer visits the same way we do any other service area, with a written quote within 24 hours.
